info.title: SvrCtlRS API
info.description: Self-hosted terminal/SSH management. Authenticate with an API token (`Authorization: Bearer svr_…`, Settings → Access) or the session cookie. Errors use the `ErrorBody` envelope. The terminal WebSocket (`/ws/terminal/pty`) is described in docs/API.md.

get.summary: The caller's requests, newest first (signed-in users only)

One request; with `?wait=N`, answers when it is decided or after N seconds (≤ 25).
Readable by the owner's tokens, so the asker can wait for the answer.

parameters.name: wait
parameters.description: Seconds to wait for a decision before answering (at most 25)

post.summary: Approve: the held call runs now, as the token that asked (signed-in owner only)

200.description: Decided; `result` is what the call answered

post.summary: Deny: nothing runs (signed-in owner only)

get.summary: Newest first; `next_before` is the cursor for the following page, null on the last one.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text in the action, target, details, user, address or token name

post.summary:
Trade the one-time code from the browser, and the PKCE verifier only the app holds, for a
session token (`Authorization: Bearer <session_id>`, 30 days). The token is the app's; the
browser's session is not touched.

200.description: Signed in; `session_id` is the app's Bearer token

400.description: Unknown, used or expired code, or the wrong verifier (`APP_CODE_INVALID`)

429.description: Too many failures from this address

post.summary:
JSON login handler for Tauri/SPA clients (no redirect, returns JSON). An account with
two-factor sign-in on also needs `totp` (a code or a recovery code); without it the answer
is 401 with `code: TOTP_REQUIRED`.

200.description: Signed in; the session cookie is set too

401.description: Wrong password, or a code is required (`TOTP_REQUIRED`) or wrong (`TOTP_INVALID`)

post.summary:
Mint a one-time WebSocket ticket for the authenticated caller (and the API token it came
with, whose access the upgrade then has).

200.description: Use as `?ticket=` on `/ws/terminal/pty` within 30 s, once

403.description: The token's preset has no terminal

get.summary: One of the caller's recordings; anyone else's is 404

delete.summary:
Delete a finished recording and its file. One still being written is refused: end the
session first, so the recorder is not left writing to a deleted file.

The recording as plain asciicast v2, decrypted as it streams. A recording still being

get.summary: List all servers

post.summary: Create a new server

Create servers from the `Host` blocks of an `ssh_config`. Names that already exist are
skipped; `ProxyJump` becomes `via_server_id` when its first hop names a created or existing
server (by name, else by hostname). Nothing is connected to.

Add a server and get it to a trusted key: create it with a stored credential as the way
in, confirm its host key (only with the fingerprint you compared on the host), check the
login, then generate a key here, install it with the way in, prove it and switch to it.
Stops at the first step that needs you, saying what to do; run it again to continue (a
server of the same name and hostname is picked up). `dry_run` changes nothing.

200.description: How far it got; `next` says what to do when not `done`

409.description: A server of that name has another hostname

get.summary: Get server by ID

202.description: Held for the owner's approval (a token set to ask first)

post.summary:
Install a key credential's public half on the server using one-time bootstrap access,
verify that the key now logs in, and make it the server's credential.

400.description: Bootstrap failed, or the key does not log in

post.summary:
Why svrctlrs can or cannot reach the server: DNS, TCP (or the jump host's tunnel), the SSH
handshake, the host key and the login, per hop, with a fix for the first failure. Runs from
where svrctlrs runs. A first contact records the presented key as unconfirmed.

Run one command on the server through its stored credential, without a terminal, and
return its output and exit status. Audited with the command as typed: keep secrets out of
command lines.

400.description: Bad request, or the connection failed

get.summary: List a directory on the server

delete.summary: Delete a file, or an empty directory. Nothing recursive: that belongs in the shell.

get.summary: The file's bytes, streamed, as a download.

put.summary: Create or overwrite a file with the request body, streamed.

post.summary: Make a folder
Rename or move; an existing destination is a 409

get.summary:
SSH host keys recorded for a server, with OpenSSH-style fingerprints (no key material):
the trusted ones, and the unconfirmed one from a first contact, if any.

delete.summary:
Forget every host key recorded for a server. The next connection records the key it sees
and asks for confirmation again; do this after the server's key legitimately changed.

202.description: Held for the owner's approval (a token set to ask first)

post.summary:
Trust the host key recorded on first contact, identified by the fingerprint the user saw
(so a key that changed between showing and confirming is not trusted by accident). 404 when
no unconfirmed key with that fingerprint is waiting (connect once to record it).

Replace the server's key: check the current one logs in, generate a new key here, install
it with the current one, prove it, switch, and remove the old public key from the server's
`authorized_keys`. The old credential is kept (other servers may use it). `dry_run`
changes nothing.

200.description: How far it got; `next` says what to do

400.description: The server does not log in with a stored key

post.summary:
Test server SSH connection. Always 200: `success` says how it went, and a failure carries
the error's `code` and `details` (the fingerprint to confirm, on first contact).

get.summary:
The caller's live shells, attached or waiting to be resumed, and how long they are kept.
Kept shells (tmux) from before a restart are listed too, as `waiting`: attaching to one
reconnects it.

put.summary:
Choose how long your shells are kept with nobody attached: one of `detach_ttl_choices`
from `GET /sessions`, or null for the server's default. Shells already waiting are kept
that long from now.

delete.summary:
End the shell behind a session, attached or not (a kept shell waiting after a restart
too: its tmux session is ended on the server).

get.summary: All settings, grouped by the part of the key before the first dot

put.summary:
Update several settings at once (upsert each). A secret key with an empty value is left
untouched, so a form can resend everything without knowing the stored token.

post.summary: Create a new setting

get.summary: One setting

put.summary: Update (or create) a setting value — upsert behavior

get.summary: Server status endpoint
The caller's tokens, newest first, revoked and expired ones included

post.summary: Create a token; the response is the only place its secret appears

409.description: You already have a token with that name

put.summary: Turn approvals on or off for one of the caller's tokens.

delete.summary: Remove a token, whatever its state

post.summary: Revoke a token now; terminals opened with it close

get.summary: Every account

post.summary: Create an account (signed-in users only; no token can)

delete.summary:
Unlink one of the caller's provider identities. With password sign-in off, the last one
stays (it is the only way in).

409.description: The last way to sign in

put.summary:
Change the caller's own password; the current password is required so a hijacked session
alone cannot lock the owner out.

400.description: The new password is too short

get.summary: The caller's own preference document under `key`; `value` is null until they save one.

put.summary: Replace the caller's own preference document under `key` (a JSON object, at most 16 KiB).

get.summary: How the caller can sign in, and how this server lets anyone sign in

post.summary:
Start turning on two-factor sign-in: a new secret for the authenticator app. Nothing
changes for sign-in until a code from it is confirmed.

Finish turning on two-factor sign-in with a code from the app; answers the recovery codes,
once.
Turn two-factor sign-in off (the recovery codes go with it)
Ten new recovery codes in place of the old ones

delete.summary: Delete an account: not your own, not the last one (signed-in users only)

ApiToken.description: A token as listed: never its secret or hash.

prefix.description: `svr_` and the first six characters of the secret

require_approval.description: Deleting a server or credential, or forgetting host keys, waits for the owner's yes

AppTokenRequest.description:
`POST /auth/app-token`: the desktop app trades the one-time code its loopback port received
from the browser, and the PKCE verifier only it holds, for a session token.

id.description: Random; it is in the link

url.description: Where the owner approves or denies it, signed in

ApprovalChannelTest.description:
`POST /notifications/test-approval`: where approval requests would go, unsaved; an empty
secret is the saved one.

AuditEntry.description: One thing someone did. Entries never hold secrets and outlive deleted users.

username.description: The account's current name while it exists, else the name at the time

details.description: A JSON object, as a string

token_id.description: The API token the request came in with

token_name.description: That token's name at the time

AuditPage.description: One page of the log, newest first.

next_before.description: Pass as `before` for the next page; null on the last one

AuthorizeKey.description:
`POST /servers/{id}/authorize-key`: install a key credential's public half with one-time
access, verify it, and switch the server to it

password.description: One-time bootstrap: the account's password (never stored) …

bootstrap_credential_id.description: … or a credential that already works on the server

removed.description: Older copies removed to stay within `keep`

BackupFile.description: A copy in the backup folder.

removed.description: Older copies retention removed after this one

error.description: Why it failed; null when it wrote a copy

BackupStatus.description:
`GET /backups`: where copies go, when the next one runs, what happened last, and the
copies that exist.

keep.description: Copies kept (`backup.keep`); 0 means nightly backups are off

hour.description: Hour of the day, UTC, the nightly copy runs (`backup.hour`)

next_run.description: When the next nightly copy is due; null when they are off

key_source.description: Where the encryption key comes from: `environment` or `file`. Backups never hold it.

running.description: A copy is being written right now

oneOf.description: The latest attempt, whatever its outcome
The latest attempt that wrote a copy

files.description: The copies in the folder, newest first

details.description:
On failure only (null when there are none): what a client can act on, such as the
`fingerprint` to confirm

CreatedToken.description: What `POST /tokens` answers: the only time the secret is shown.

secret.description: `svr_` + 40 letters and digits; send it as `Authorization: Bearer …`

passphrase.description: Omit to keep the current passphrase; an empty string removes it

CredentialDetail.description: One credential (value redacted; an SSH key's public half included).

CredentialSummary.description: A credential in the list (values redacted).

username.description: The login it comes with, if any

key_source.description: SSH keys: `key` (material stored here) or `path` (a file on the server)

fingerprint.description: SSH keys: `SHA256:…` of the public half

in_use.description: Some server uses it (deleting it is refused)

used_by.description: The names of the servers that use it

credential_id.description:
Log in with this stored credential instead of the server's own, to test it (for
example that a rotated-away key no longer works) without changing the server. The
server's recorded status is left alone.

Diagnosis.description:
`POST /servers/{id}/diagnose`: why svrctlrs can or cannot reach a server, step by step,
from where svrctlrs runs (its container, address, DNS and credentials).

ok.description: Every step passed: a shell would open

verdict.description: One sentence: what is wrong, or that all is well

hops.description: The jump hosts in order, then the server itself

fix.description: What to do about a failure

modified.description: RFC 3339, when the server reported a modification time

details.description: Extras a client can act on (for example the fingerprint of an unconfirmed host key)

ExecRequest.description: `POST /servers/{id}/exec`: one command, no terminal, through the stored credential.

exit_code.description: Null when the command was still running at the deadline

stdout_truncated.description: More than 1 MiB came out on that stream; the rest was dropped

GenerateKey.description:
`POST /credentials/generate-key`: an ed25519 key made on the server; the private half
never leaves it.

comment.description: Comment at the end of the public key line (default `svrctlrs:<name>`)

Health.description: `GET /health`: unauthenticated; 503 with `status: degraded` when the database is down.

revision.description: The git commit the image was built from; `unknown` outside CI builds

HostKey.description: A host key recorded for a server (no key material).

trusted_at.description: Null for the key seen on first contact, waiting for confirmation

IdMessage.description: `{ "id": 3, "message": "…" }`: what a create, update or delete of a numbered row answers.

notes.description: Jump hosts set, and ones that could not be

email.description: What the provider said at the last sign-in

Listing.description: `GET /servers/{id}/files`: directories first, then names ignoring case.

path.description: The directory listed, resolved (home is shown as its real path)

LoggedIn.description: A successful login: the session id doubles as a Bearer token for native apps.

totp.description: A TOTP code or a recovery code, for an account with two-factor sign-in on

LoginRefused.description: A refused login (this route predates the error envelope)

code.description: `TOTP_REQUIRED` (send `totp` too) or `TOTP_INVALID`; absent for other refusals

value.description: The password, or OpenSSH private key material (or a key path on the server)

passphrase.description: Passphrase of an encrypted SSH key

pane_configs.description: JSON array of `{server_id}` objects, one per pane

via_server_id.description: Reach this server through another server's SSH connection (jump host)

startup_command.description: One line typed into every new shell, e.g. `tmux new -A -s main`

is_local.description: Retired with command mode; `true` is refused

expires_in_days.description: Required: 1–3650 days, or null for a token that never expires

NotificationTest.description:
`POST /notifications/test`: values from the form, unsaved; absent ones are the saved
settings, and an empty token is the saved token.

credential_id.description:
The way in: a credential stored in svrctlrs that already works there (a password or
a key). Passwords and private keys never travel in this request.

fingerprint.description: The `SHA256:` fingerprint you compared on the host; it is trusted only if it matches

new_key.description: Generate a key here, install it with the way in, and switch to it (default true)

dry_run.description: Say what would happen, change nothing

server_id.description: Null in a dry run, or when nothing was created

next.description: What to do next, when not done

OpStep.description: One step of an onboarding or key rotation.

PasswordConfirmation.description: The caller's current password, for changes that could lock them out

Preference.description: One of the caller's preference documents (`terminal`); `value` is null until saved.

value.description: A JSON object the UI owns

PreferenceValue.description: `PUT /users/me/preferences/{key}`: a JSON object of at most 16 KiB

pane_configs.description: A JSON array of `{server_id}` objects, one per pane, as a string

server_id.description: Only offered on this server, when set

Recording.description: One recorded shell (asciicast v2, encrypted at rest; `GET /recordings/{id}/cast` streams it).

server_id.description: Null once the server is deleted; `server_name` keeps what it was called

cols.description: Terminal size when the recording started; resizes are events in the file

size_bytes.description: Plaintext asciicast bytes written so far (the size of a download)

end_reason.description: Why it ended: the shell's exit, the size limit, the error

retention_days.description: Recordings older than this are deleted; 0 keeps them

max_bytes.description: A recording stops at this size and the shell goes on unrecorded

RecoveryCodes.description: Ten one-time recovery codes. Shown once; only their hashes are kept.

RotateKeyRequest.description:
`POST /servers/{id}/rotate-key`: generate a new key, install it with the current one,
prove it, switch, and remove the old public key from the server.

remove_old.description: Remove the old public key from `authorized_keys` (default true)

username.description: SSH user; null means the credential's user, else `root`

via_server_id.description: Reached through this server's SSH connection (a jump host)

tags.description: Labels for filtering: trimmed, unique ignoring case, sorted

startup_command.description: Typed into every new shell right after it starts (one line)

record_sessions.description: Shells opened here are recorded for the user who opens them

persistent_shell.description:
New shells run in tmux on the server, so they outlive a restart of SvrCtlRS (a server
without tmux gets a plain shell and a note)

credential_id.description: Absent keeps the credential, `null` unassigns it, a number sets it

via_server_id.description: Absent keeps it, `null` makes the server direct again

SessionKeep.description: The caller's keep time after a change.

SessionKeepUpdate.description: `PUT /sessions/keep`: how long the caller's shells are kept with nobody attached.

detach_ttl_secs.description: One of `detach_ttl_choices`, or null for the server's default
How long the caller's shells are kept with nobody attached

detach_ttl_choices.description: The lengths the caller can choose from (`PUT /sessions/keep`), within the maximum

detach_ttl_chosen.description: The caller chose `detach_ttl_secs`; false means the server's default

SessionSummary.description: A shell the server holds for the caller, attached or not.

persistent.description: It runs in tmux on the server and outlives a restart of SvrCtlRS

waiting.description: Kept in tmux but not connected since SvrCtlRS restarted; attaching reconnects it

Setting.description:
One setting. Secret ones (`notification.token`, `approval.matrix_token`,
`approval.webhook_url`) read back with an empty `value` and `is_set`.

is_set.description: Whether a value is stored (the only thing a secret setting tells)

SettingSaved.description: What a create or update of one setting answers

SettingsList.description: `GET /settings`: settings grouped by the part of the key before the first dot

SettingsUpdate.description: `PUT /settings`: several at once; a secret key with an empty value is left as it is

updated.description: The keys written (secrets sent empty are not)

password_login.description: Whether this server accepts a password at all (`PASSWORD_LOGIN`)

oneOf.description: The OpenID Connect provider this server signs in with, if one is configured

identities.description: The caller's identities at that provider (or at one configured before)

TotpEnrolment.description:
`POST /users/me/totp`: what to load into the authenticator app. Shown once; the secret is
not readable again.

secret.description: Base32, for typing in by hand

qr_svg.description: The URI as an SVG QR code

enabled.description: A password sign-in also asks for a code

fingerprint.description: The fingerprint you compared with `ssh-keygen -lf` on the host

UserAccount.description: An account. Password hashes never leave the server.

last_login_at.description: The most recent successful login in the audit log

WsTicket.description: `POST /auth/ws-ticket`: one use, on a WebSocket upgrade only (`?ticket=`).
